extracted.intended_audience: web developers, site maintainers, and accessibility engineers integrating MathJax/MathML into websites
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for making mathematical content accessible on the web using MathJax (version 2.7), including UI accessibility, accessibility extensions, legacy AssistiveMML support, and platform-specific notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: MathJax Menu follows WCAG 2.0
rubrics_metrics.description: The MathJax Menu follows WCAG 2.0 guidelines: each MathJax fragment is included in the tab order; the menu can be triggered via the space or menu key; and navigation in the menu is possible using the arrow keys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The UI is localized to many languages. Ensure math fragments are focusable (in tab order) and that keyboard triggers (space/menu key) and arrow-key navigation are implemented so users relying on keyboard or AT can open and navigate the MathJax menu.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localize MathJax User Interface
rubrics_metrics.description: The MathJax user interface is localized to over 20 languages and supports partial localizations via community contributions (TranslateWiki.net).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide appropriate localization strings for the MathJax menu and processing messages to improve usability for non-English users; leverage community localization resources where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the MathJax Accessibility Extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: MathJax provides Accessibility extensions that offer several tools and features enabling universal rendering of mathematics on the web; these extensions enhance rendering both visually and aurally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The documentation strongly suggests using the Accessibility extensions to provide the best possible experience for all users — enable them by default on pages where accessibility is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsive rendering through collapsing and exploration of subexpressions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Accessibility extensions provide an innovative responsive rendering of mathematical content through collapsing and exploration of subexpressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable collapsing/exploration to allow users to inspect complex expressions piece-by-piece; this supports comprehension for users who cannot perceive full expressions at once.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aural rendering (on-the-fly speech-text) using rule sets
rubrics_metrics.description: An aural rendering tool provides on-the-fly speech-text for mathematical content and its subexpressions using various rule sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Configure appropriate speech rule sets for target audiences/locale so screenreaders receive meaningful, rule-governed speech output rather than raw character strings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploration tool with highlighting and synchronized aural rendering
rubrics_metrics.description: An exploration tool allows meaningful exploration of mathematical content including multiple highlighting features and synchronized aural rendering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the exploration features to let users step through expressions visually and aurally in sync; enable highlighting so users can see which subexpression is being read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rely on well-supported web standards (WAI-ARIA) for broad AT support
rubrics_metrics.description: The Accessibility Extensions support the widest selection of browsers, operating systems, and assistive technologies because they only require the use of well-supported web standards such as WAI-ARIA, in particular labels and live regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement ARIA labels and live regions correctly to maximize compatibility with screenreaders and other AT; prefer solutions that use standards rather than proprietary plugins.

rubrics_metrics.name: AssistiveMML: embed visually-hidden MathML for legacy screenreaders
rubrics_metrics.description: The AssistiveMML extension embeds visually hidden MathML alongside MathJax’s visual rendering while hiding the visual rendering from assistive technology (AT), allowing MathML-enabled screenreaders to read the underlying mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AssistiveMML where target screenreaders support MathML. Be aware that Presentation MathML is often insufficient to convey full semantic meaning; screenreaders will use heuristics and rule sets to interpret MathML.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and expected behavior of visually-hidden MathML
rubrics_metrics.description: Given current technology, the expected result when using AssistiveMML is: the visually-hidden MathML is read out correctly by AT (not just character strings, e.g., <mfrac> leads to 'fraction' — subject to screenreader MathML support); the visual rendering is not read out by AT; the MathJax Menu triggers AT to say 'clickable' before each math element; visually-hidden MathML does not get an outline (usually placed oddly because it is visually hidden) except on iOS VoiceOver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test target screenreaders to confirm they map MathML elements into semantic speech. Do not assume consistent behavior across platforms; adjust markup or provide alternative cues where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult the Support Matrix for AssistiveMML compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A support matrix summarizes results for MathML-enabled screenreaders and the legacy AssistiveMML extension (usable? bugs) for specific combinations of screenreader, browser, and OS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult this matrix (and test) to determine whether a given screenreader/browser/OS combo will be usable with AssistiveMML; do not assume universal support. Use the matrix to plan fallbacks or to advise users about supported setups.

rubrics_metrics.name: VoiceOver has browser-specific MathML behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes on Apple VoiceOver: on OSX+Safari the visually-hidden MathML is read and gets an outline but VoiceOver sometimes drops parts of equations; on Chrome the visually-hidden MathML is detected but often not read correctly (e.g., '4 items detected; math'); on Firefox the visually-hidden MathML may be read only as a string of characters; on iOS manual exploration and the two-finger gesture can read visually-hidden MathML, but tapping may not work because the MathML is placed in a 1px box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect inconsistent and partial MathML support across browsers with VoiceOver. Test the specific browser/OS combination used by your audience and provide guidance or fallbacks (e.g., enable exploration mode) for iOS users because tapping may not access equations.

rubrics_metrics.name: MathPlayer 4 and Internet Explorer 11 caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Design Science recommends using IE’s Enterprise mode for MathPlayer in IE11 for visual rendering and that MathPlayer requires the MathPlayer BrowserHelperAddon; however, the BrowserHelperAddon can lead to crashes (e.g., switching to NativeMML output can crash IE11 and require clearing MathJax cookies). Using Enterprise mode may be required for MathPlayer visual rendering, but several interactions can break other functionality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid switching on IE Enterprise mode or using the MathPlayer BrowserHelperAddon on pages using MathJax where possible. If MathPlayer/IE11 must be supported, follow vendor docs carefully and be prepared to advise users about instability and to provide recovery steps (clear MathJax cookie).
